why: Pre-workout plus coffee plus energy drinks is common in gym culture here. A 'count your milligrams' thread is useful and invites people to share their numbers.

title: New AHA abstract on energy drinks and stimulant pre-workouts. Has anyone actually added up their daily caffeine in mg?
text:
The American Heart Association released a preliminary study this month. Researchers went through more than 28,000 FDA adverse event reports from 2017 to 2025, and heart events like cardiac arrest showed up far more often with energy drinks and stimulant products than with non-stimulant products. About 45% of those reports involved people aged 18 to 34.

It's an abstract, not peer reviewed yet, and reports like these can't tell you how common the problem is or which ingredient did it. Industry groups have already pushed back on that.

Still, it made me add up a normal gym day for a friend: two coffees, a pre-workout with 200 to 300 mg, sometimes an energy drink before an evening session. That gets close to or past the 400 mg a day that regulators usually cite for healthy adults.

What does your day look like in milligrams? And has anyone cut pre-workout and noticed a difference in sleep or resting heart rate?

(Disclosure: I run a small supplement company, so weigh my take accordingly. No products or links in this post.)
